explanation: For each position i, choose uniformly among positions i through n-1 and exchange the chosen value into position i.
correctness: At position i each remaining occurrence has probability 1/(n-i) of being selected. Multiplying conditional probabilities gives 1/n! for each full occurrence permutation.
walkthrough: Starting with [4,8,1], position 0 chooses uniformly among all three occurrences. If it selects index 2, the array becomes [1,8,4]. Position 1 then chooses index 1 or 2 equally, producing [1,8,4] or [1,4,8]. Each full three-element permutation has probability 1/(3*2)=1/6. The judge returns true when these distribution and in-place properties hold. The callable mutates the supplied array and returns void/None/undefined. Expected true is the checker verdict for occurrence preservation, identity, legal source use and unbiased permutations; it is not a particular array result.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays remain unchanged. Repeated values are separate occurrences; unbiased occurrence permutations may have the same visible value sequence.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: a constant-time random choice and swap fixes one position per iteration.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: only indices and a swap temporary; all rearrangement uses the original array.
